skill.name: browser-use
skill.description: Direct browser control via CDP for web interaction: automation, scraping, testing, screenshots, and site/app work.
skill.summary: Control local or cloud browsers through CDP for visual interaction, inspection, automation, scraping, and testing.
skill.author: browser-use

security_audit.summary: All static detections are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation links, expected API-key authentication, and local screenshot capture. The skill still introduces risk by loading optional host-specific instructions and allowing automatic SSO in an authenticated browser. Publish only with clearer trust and consent boundaries.

remediation.issue: Host-specific domain skills are loaded without documented trust or integrity checks.
remediation.suggestion: Use an allowlist, verify file ownership or integrity, and request confirmation before loading instructions from host-matched directories.

remediation.issue: The login workflow permits automatic SSO when Chrome already has an authenticated session.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before starting SSO, and display the target site and selected account before authorization.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Tasks with Direct CDP Control
content.value_statement: Complex browser tasks often require visual checks, precise interaction, and reliable session control. This skill connects Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to local and cloud browsers through CDP.
actual_capabilities: Control local Chrome or Chromium through CDP using the browser-use command and pre-imported helpers.
Open tabs, navigate pages, wait for loads, inspect the DOM with JavaScript, and send raw CDP commands.
Capture screenshots and click coordinates for visual interaction across iframes, shadow DOM, and cross-origin content.
Start named cloud browser daemons for isolated or parallel tasks, then stop them after use.
Run connection diagnostics and guide users through enabling Chrome remote debugging.
Load optional host-specific domain skills when the feature is explicitly enabled.
limitations: Local control requires the browser-use command, a compatible Chrome or Chromium browser, and remote debugging permission.
Cloud sessions require Browser Use authentication and may incur charges until stopped or timed out.
Coordinate-based clicks depend on current pixels and require screenshot checks after page changes.
Detailed interaction and domain guidance is referenced from external repository files rather than included here.

use_cases.title: Verify Web Workflows
use_cases.description: Inspect pages, capture visual state, perform controlled interactions, and confirm outcomes in a real browser session.

use_cases.title: Collect Structured Web Findings
use_cases.description: Navigate research sources, inspect page content, and summarize relevant information with screenshots when visual evidence matters.

use_cases.title: Run Isolated Browser Tasks
use_cases.description: Create separate cloud browsers for concurrent automation jobs that should not share tabs, focus, cookies, or browsing state.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], wait for the page to load, capture a screenshot, and summarize the visible content. Do not click or submit anything.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], inspect the form fields, and report required information and validation rules. Stop before entering sensitive data or submitting.

prompt_templates.title: Test a User Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Test this workflow: [STEPS]. Capture screenshots before important actions, wait after navigation, and report failures with the visible page state.

prompt_templates.title: Run Parallel Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Use separate named cloud browsers to research [TOPICS] concurrently. Keep each session isolated, summarize findings, and ask before leaving any browser running.

output_examples.input: Inspect the pricing page and identify the available plans without starting checkout.
output: The page shows three plans with monthly and annual billing options.
Each plan lists its included usage limits and support level.

output_examples.input: Test whether the account page opens while the browser is already signed in.
output_examples.output: The account page loaded successfully and displayed the current profile. No password, MFA, consent, or account selection prompt appeared.

output_examples.input: Check a multi-step form and stop before final submission.
output: All required fields were identified across three steps.
The second step rejected an invalid date and displayed a clear validation message.
The final submission button was not selected.

best_practices: Capture a screenshot before coordinate clicks and capture another screenshot immediately after the action.
Ask before entering credentials, approving consent, choosing an ambiguous account, or leaving a billable cloud browser running.
Use one named cloud browser per parallel task and keep the same name for every command in that session.
anti_patterns: Do not use stale screenshots or coordinates after navigation, scrolling, resizing, or major page updates.
Do not start a named remote daemon and continue sending commands to the default daemon.
Do not load host-specific domain instructions from untrusted or user-writable locations without review.

faq.question: What browser connection does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the Chrome DevTools Protocol through a local daemon or a named Browser Use cloud browser.

faq.question: Does local Chrome require permission?
faq.answer: Yes. Chrome remote debugging must be enabled, and the user may need to approve the browser permission prompt.

faq.question: Can it run multiple browser tasks at once?
faq.answer: Yes. Separate named cloud browsers can isolate concurrent tasks that would otherwise compete for tabs and focus.

faq.question: Can it handle signed-in websites?
faq.answer: It can use an existing browser session, but credentials, MFA, consent, and ambiguous account choices require user involvement.

faq.question: Does it support screenshots and DOM inspection?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports screenshot capture, coordinate clicks, JavaScript inspection, and raw CDP commands.

faq.question: Are cloud browsers free to leave running?
faq.answer: No. Remote browsers may continue billing until stopped or timed out, so the skill should ask before leaving them active.
